newsitem.title: UK: Explosion and bomb warnings hit northern England.
newsitem.headline: Explosion and bomb warnings hit northern England.

text.p: An explosion at a railway station and bomb warnings affecting the main north/south rail lines brought chaos to northern England and Prime Minister John Major said he believed they were the work of the IRA.

Britain's railway operator Railtrack said there had been a small explosion at the station in the city of Leeds. Police also carried out a controlled explosions at Stoke railway station in northwest England.
There were no reports of injuries.
Police declined to confirm media reports which said the explosion was on the railway line at Leeds.

Major pinned the incidents on the Irish Republican Army (IRA) which is battling to end Britain's rule of Northern Ireland and has admitted causing rail and road disruption earlier in Britain's campaign for a May 1 general election.
"This looks very much at the moment as though this is the work of the IRA showing their usual contempt for people's lives and for property," Major told his daily news conference.
Earlier, police said they had received bomb warnings using a recognised code word which forced them to close four major railway stations and the M6 motorway.
This closed off the main rail and traffic links between the north and south of Britain, bringing huge disruption to the north of England.
"A local organisation received a warning at 7:10 this morning using a codeword similar to one used before," said a spokeswoman for Cheshire police, responsible for vital Crewe railway station.
She said the station and the surrounding area had been evacuated. "There is major disruption here," she said.
Last month, two bombs exploded near Wilmslow railway station in northwest England, but no-one was injured, and Semtex bombs were planted on the M6.
The Irish Republican Army claimed responsibility for the attacks and threats, which paralysed northwest England.

The IRA also claimed responsibility for a bomb warning that halted the Grand National horse race earlier this month and bomb threats at London railway stations have brought chaos to the capital several times in the past few weeks.
